title: Local sums identify traces under etale localization
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be finite etale and $g:X^{\prime}\to X$ etale [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $Y^{\prime}=Y\times_XX^{\prime}$ and $f^{\prime}:Y^{\prime}\to X^{\prime}$, and for an abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ put $F^{\prime}=g^{-1}F$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Suppose $\tau:f_*f^{-1}F\to F$ and $\tau^{\prime}:f^{\prime}_*(f^{\prime})^{-1}F^{\prime}\to F^{\prime}$ both satisfy their local sum predicates [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-local-sums]. For every object $W$ over $X^{\prime}$ and every pasting isomorphism $\kappa_W:W\times_{X^{\prime}}Y^{\prime}\simeq W\times_XY$ whose projections are $\mathrm{id}_W$ and the projection to $Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting], the transported trace components satisfy $\rho^g_F(W)\circ\overline\tau^{\prime}_W=\overline\tau_W\circ F(\kappa_W^{-1})\circ\rho^g_F(W\times_{X^{\prime}}Y^{\prime})$. Here $\rho^g_F:g^{-1}F\simeq F|_{X^{\prime}}$ and each bar denotes composition with the inverse restriction isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. No relationship between the choices of $\tau$ and $\tau^{\prime}$ is assumed beyond these predicates.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: The pullback $f^{\prime}$ is finite etale. For each $W$ over $X^{\prime}$ choose an etale jointly surjective covering on which its pullback of $Y^{\prime}$ splits; use finite etale local splitting and covering base change. Regard its members as objects over $X$ by composition.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: Transport each splitting across the pullback pasting isomorphism. Its two projection identities show that the transported section has exactly the identity projection to the covering object and the same map to $Y$; the pullback universal property identifies the sections in the two descriptions. Transport along the inverse preserves the clopen coproduct and the inverse identities.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: On a covering member apply both local sum hypotheses. Naturality of $g^{-1}F\simeq F|_{X^{\prime}}$ makes restriction along each transported section commute with its components. Therefore the two displayed maps are the same finite sum on that member.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: Naturality of both sheaf morphisms, of the restriction isomorphism, and of the pasting maps makes these equalities exactly the restrictions of the desired component equality at $W$. For each input section use separatedness of $F|_{X^{\prime}}$ on the covering to get equality at $W$, then use extensionality of group homomorphisms. Empty objects and empty splittings are included by the empty-cover sheaf condition.
